summary: Iter 16 — Doctor Dashboard Enhancements (Task A). 12/12 backend tests PASS (test_iter16_doctor_dashboard.py). Frontend: all four new/updated screens render cleanly with correct testIDs and graceful error states. HOWEVER a CRITICAL blocker was found in POST /api/appointments/{appt_id}/prescription: the auth check `user['id'] not in (appt.patient_id, appt.doctor_id)` compares the doctor's JWT user-id against `appt.doctor_id` which is the `doctors` collection row id (NOT the user id). Confirmed via mongo: user.id=d4c8b71e… vs appt.doctor_id=01bec25e… (doctors.id). Result: the brand-new Doctor `Write Rx` flow (frontend /doctor/prescription/[apptId] → api.addPrescription) will ALWAYS receive HTTP 403 'Not allowed'. Documented in test_BUG_doctor_cannot_write_rx which currently asserts on 403 and MUST be flipped to 200 after the fix. Structured medicines_structured composition, symptoms/advice/follow_up persistence and /api/prescriptions listing all work correctly when the caller is the patient (or any role whose id happens to match). Earnings endpoint returns the correct shape with dense 30-day daily array and proper 403 for patient role. Patient-history endpoint correctly returns 403 for no-treatment-relationship and full patient+stats+appointments payload after a booking. Frontend earnings, patient-detail and prescription editor pages all render without crashes even when the API returns 401/404 — friendly error boxes shown as designed. Doctor home hero + `dh-open-earnings` earnings card + `dh-earn-tile` quick-action tiles all present. PDF export button (rx-export) is wired and visible. Deprecated web warnings 'shadow* → boxShadow' and 'expo-notifications web listener' are pre-existing dev-only warnings (non-blocking).

critical.issue: Doctor-role callers always receive 403 'Not allowed'. Root cause (/app/backend/server.py:386): `if user['id'] not in (appt.get('patient_id'), appt.get('doctor_id'))`. `appt.doctor_id` stores `doctors.id` (see line 329), NOT the doctor's user id, so the JWT user['id'] can never match. This BLOCKS the new /doctor/prescription/[apptId] editor's Save button end-to-end.

minor.issue: Same class of bug at server.py:363 — for doctor role the query is `{'doctor_id': user['id']}` but stored doctor_id is `doctors.id`. Pre-existing; doctor uses /doctor/my-appointments instead (line 1973) which resolves the row correctly. Worth aligning.

server.py:520 & :523 compare `user['id']` to `appt.doctor_id` (same user-id vs doctors-row-id mismatch). Doctor joining a video session by appointment_id may be misclassified as non-owner. Pre-existing.

integration_issues.issue: Save button will trigger api.addPrescription → 403 'Not allowed' every time because of the backend auth-check bug above. UI will show the error line but the doctor can never save. Retest after backend fix.

react_native_issues.issue: 'shadow*' style props are deprecated — use 'boxShadow'. Pre-existing web-only dev warning, does not affect Android/iOS native build.

action_items: [CRITICAL] Fix /app/backend/server.py:381 add_prescription auth check. Replace `if user['id'] not in (appt.get('patient_id'), appt.get('doctor_id')):` with a doctor-row-aware check, e.g.: `doctor_row = await db.doctors.find_one({'user_id': user['id']}, {'id':1,'_id':0}) if user['role']=='doctor' else None; allowed_ids = {appt.get('patient_id'), appt.get('doctor_id'), doctor_row['id'] if doctor_row else None}; if user['id'] != appt.get('patient_id') and (not doctor_row or doctor_row['id'] != appt.get('doctor_id')): raise 403`. Then flip test_BUG_doctor_cannot_write_rx assertion to `== 200`.

[MEDIUM] Same fix for GET /appointments list_appointments (server.py:363) and video/session ownership check (server.py:520-523). Doctor should look up their doctors row and query `{'doctor_id': doctor_row['id']}`.
[LOW] Consider storing `author_role` on the prescription doc to disambiguate patient-authored vs doctor-authored records once the doctor path starts working.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:329 stores `appt.doctor_id = doctor['id']` (doctors row id). Downstream code in three places (list_appointments L363, add_prescription L386, video/session L520-523) compares this to `user['id']` — always fails for doctor role. Only /doctor/my-appointments (L1973) does it right by resolving the doctors row first. Pattern needs to be applied consistently.

add_prescription happily accepts a patient writing a prescription for themselves — kept per the 'MVP demo flexibility' comment, but this is a real data-integrity risk in production (any patient can insert a 'prescription' on their own booking). Recommend restricting to doctors and admins post-MVP.

PrescriptionInput.medicines defaults to '' — combined with the auto-compose fallback, a caller who sends structured meds but non-empty stray whitespace in `medicines` will skip composition. Current check `.strip()` handles this correctly. ✅
MedicineItem.instructions is Optional but the auto-compose code at server.py:397 uses `m.get('instructions')` — safe because body.dict() serializes None → key present with None value. ✅

rca_of_issue: PrescriptionInput enhancement enabled multi-medicine structured Rx from a new full-screen doctor editor, but the pre-existing auth guard in add_prescription (server.py:386) was NOT updated to resolve the doctors row when the caller is a doctor. It compares JWT `user['id']` (users.id) to `appt.doctor_id` (doctors.id) — two different UUIDs. Confirmed via mongo query in this test run. Mitigation: resolve `doctor_row = doctors.find_one({user_id: user.id})` for role=='doctor' and check membership against `{appt.patient_id, appt.doctor_id, doctor_row.id}`. Reproduction: login as doctor1@vaidhyaji.example.com, book any appt as patient, POST /api/appointments/{id}/prescription with valid body — get 403 'Not allowed'. Frontend impact: /doctor/prescription/[apptId] Save button will always error out.
